answer: Each identity on the garden board audits three work samples from others before its signal is counted at dawn. Each duty locks a 50-credit bond; the registry plants one defective sample per queue, and passing it burns the bond, bars the auditor, and doubles its next bond. One garden queue cannot serve two identities, so the k-th fake needs a fresh queue and a fresh 50 locked; 1,000 fakes lock 50,000 and must clear 3,000 audits. A rubber-stamp ring fails its planted defects, losing every bond, while an honest agent audits three samples once, keeps its bond, and is counted at dawn.
